_README: PLEASE READ BEFORE TRUSTING ANYTHING THIS FILE DRIVES.
This is NOT a pollen measurement. Pune has no live open pollen-count feed.
Nothing here tells you what is in the air on any given day.
What it is: a list of tree species that are NAMED AS AEROALLERGENS IN THE
PUBLISHED INDIAN ALLERGY LITERATURE, cross-referenced against the species
the PMC census actually recorded in Pune, and against the months the census
records those species as flowering.
So the honest claim the site makes is narrow and checkable:
'These species are recorded as flowering in Pune this month, and these
ones appear in the Indian aeroallergen literature.'
It is NOT:
- a pollen count
- a forecast
- an air quality index
- medical advice, or a substitute for seeing an allergist
Actual airborne pollen on a given day depends on weather, wind, rain,
temperature and time of day, none of which is in this dataset. A tree
flowering in the census month does not mean its pollen is in the air today.
Species NOT on this list are not marked as safe. They are marked as
not-listed, which is a statement about this list, not about the tree.
Corrections welcome as a pull request against this one file.

source.title: Aeroallergens in Clinical Practice of Allergy in India — ARIA Asia Pacific Workshop Report
source.journal: Asian Pacific Journal of Allergy and Immunology, Vol 26 No 4, December 2008, p245
source.note: Tree species named in that report as aeroallergens in India. Names below are lowercased genus + species for matching, and include spelling variants as the census records them.

notable.prosopis juliflora: Identified as a major cause of pollinosis in India, with 12% of patients showing a positive skin reaction.
notable.holoptelea integrifolia: Described as an important pollen allergen of India, and among the dominant airborne types in northern India.
notable.morus alba: Among the major contributors in Delhi airborne-pollen surveys.
notable.casuarina equisetifolia: Among the dominant airborne pollen types reported in northern India.
notable.cedrus deodara: Reported as an allergen in Himalayan patients.

_showy_not_listed: The showiest flowering trees in Pune are largely insect-pollinated and do
NOT appear in the aeroallergen list above — Delonix regia (Gulmohar),
Cassia fistula (Bahava), Tabebuia, Plumeria, Spathodea. Their absence from
the list is not proof they are harmless; it means the report did not name
them. But it is why the tree that looks most dramatic in flower is often
not the one behind a streaming nose.
